title: Credit cards — use them without falling into the interest trap
publisher: Artha Kavach summary of public guidance (RBI / SEBI / IRDAI / Income Tax Dept) — pending manual verification
text: A credit card is a short-term loan that is free only if you pay the full statement amount by the due date. If you pay only the 'minimum due' or miss the date, interest is charged on the whole outstanding amount, typically about 3–4% per month (roughly 36–48% a year), plus late fees and GST — one of the most expensive forms of debt. Safe habits: treat the card as a debit card (spend only what you could pay today), set up auto-pay for the full amount, keep usage under 30% of your limit, never withdraw cash on it (interest starts immediately, with a fee), and avoid taking a card just for the reward points. If you are already stuck, pay the highest-interest card first and consider converting the balance to a lower-interest personal loan or EMI plan only after checking the total cost.
summary_hinglish: Credit card tabhi free hai jab poora bill due date tak bharo. Sirf minimum due bharoge to poori outstanding amount par lagbhag 3-4% per month (36-48% saal) byaj lagta hai. Card ko debit card ki tarah use karo, auto-pay full amount par lagao, cash withdrawal mat karo.
summary_hi: क्रेडिट कार्ड तभी मुफ़्त है जब पूरा बिल देय तिथि तक चुकाएं। सिर्फ़ मिनिमम ड्यू भरने पर पूरी बकाया रकम पर लगभग 3-4% प्रति माह (36-48% सालाना) ब्याज लगता है। कार्ड को डेबिट कार्ड की तरह इस्तेमाल करें और ऑटो-पे पूरी रकम पर रखें।
